title: [P0][capture] Unhandled client-side preprocessing failure hangs the upload UI indefinitely
goal: handleFiles's startTransition callback (app/(app)/add/capture.tsx:61-70) calls await preprocessFile(file) (HEIC conversion via heic2any, or canvas downscaling) with no try/catch. If conversion throws -- a real case for corrupt/unusual HEIC from some Android/iOS camera apps -- setStatus('idle') and setResults(...) never run, so the UI is stuck on 'Got it -- processing...' indefinitely with inputs disabled and no way to retry. In a multi-file batch, one bad file silently stalls the whole batch.
in_scope: Wrap the per-file preprocessing step in capture.tsx's handleFiles loop in try/catch.
On a caught failure, push a per-file result state ('Failed -- couldn't process image', with a retry or skip affordance) instead of leaving the batch stuck.
Ensure status always reaches 'idle' after all files in the batch have been attempted, regardless of individual failures.
Verify the rest of the batch continues processing when one file fails -- one bad HEIC must not block the others.
out_of_scope: Fixing heic2any's own conversion correctness or supporting additional image formats -- this story is about failure handling, not format coverage.
Server-side preprocessing fallback -- out of scope unless the client-side fix proves insufficient.
acceptance: A file that fails client-side preprocessing (HEIC conversion or downscaling) produces a per-file 'Failed -- couldn't process image' result with a retry affordance, and does not block status from reaching 'idle'. The rest of a multi-file batch continues processing independently of one file's failure.
invariants: A single bad file in a batch must never hang the entire upload flow -- this is the core defect and the primary regression to guard against.
The failure state must be visible to the user, not just logged -- a silent console error with a stuck spinner is the same bug from the user's perspective.
